brief: A tarot card designed as "The Wheel": its centre is a hyperreal close-up of a road bicycle hub. Polished spokes radiate, grease is caught in the cassette teeth, and a tiny reflection of sky glints in the chrome. The card is framed with a pen-drawn border of fine double lines, corner rosettes and a blank title banner at the base. The border is flat-coloured in faded vermilion, ultramarine and parchment cream. Inside it, coloured pencil achieves photographic depth, so the flat, symbolic frame contrasts with the obsessive centre. The edges are slightly worn and the corners rounded, like a much-shuffled deck.

A cantaloupe split in half on a checked picnic blanket, seen from close above. It is divided into cells by heavy, confident outlines in Prussian indigo, like leaded glass. Within each cell, the colour is laid as watercolour that reads flat from a distance but holds hyperreal gradation up close: wet orange flesh, glistening seeds, netted rind in sage and sand. The blanket squares of madder red and cream are fully enclosed by the same dark line. The style uses Synthetist simplification, but the juice droplets and the seed-cavity sheen are startlingly real.

A cel-animation split between painted background and inked foreground. Behind, a laundromat dryer drum rendered in soft, hyperreal watercolour. Tumbling towels in faded coral and mint blur with wet-in-wet bleeds, and condensation beads catch tiny lifted highlights. In front sits the chrome porthole rim and glass, treated like an acetate overlay. Crisp uniform pen contours enclose it, with shading in two hard-edged flat tones of cool grey and one white specular slash. The tension comes from the painterly, breathing interior against the clean graphic rim. The view is slightly off-axis, with the porthole cropped by the frame's right edge.

An overhead view of a neglected cast-iron skillet with a freshly fried egg. Its glossy yolk contrasts with a pan crusted in rust bloom. Watercolour carries the oxidation: burnt sienna, Mars orange and raw umber flood in and dry into hard cauliflower edges and granulating pools, like corrosion spreading across steel. Spray flecks add pitted scale. The egg white is rendered in clean, smooth pencil with crisp lacy browned edges and a single wet highlight on the yolk. The skillet handle pushes diagonally out of the frame onto a pale concrete ground.

A chubby toddler in a quilted crimson jacket hugs a real, wriggling golden carp. The composition is frontal and celebratory, like a Chinese New Year woodblock print. The palette uses nianhua's loud, flat brights: peach-pink, emerald, lemon yellow and vermilion. These are laid in marker-flat fields with thin black keylines. The toddler's flushed cheeks, wet scales, gaping fish mouth and splashed water droplets are rendered with hyperreal watercolour nuance. Auspicious cloud scrolls and lotus-free coin motifs pack the flat background. The festive symmetry is undercut by the fish's very real slipperiness.

A pair of muddy, cracked work boots stands frontally against a flat, burnished gold ground, like an icon. The boots are hyperreal: charcoal-dense leather creases, frayed laces, dried clay rendered in umber and ochre watercolour with crisp granular flakes. The gold is built from layered yellow ochre and raw sienna washes, flecked with spray to suggest leaf seams and craquelure. Fine pen lines trace tiny squares where the sheets of leaf overlap. A subtle halo arc is incised above the boots. The light is sacred and even, yet the subject is stubbornly humble.

An extreme horizontal close-up of four bass guitar strings running edge to edge across a rosewood neck. The windings, finger grime and fret wire are rendered photographically through fine directional hatching that flows along each string. The colour behaves like a spectrogram heatmap. The low strings glow deep violet and magma red, rising through orange to pale yellow on the highest. The vertical frets read as time markers. A blurred plucking fingertip enters from the bottom edge, and its shimmer smears colour sideways.

An elderly woman sits cross-legged at the exact centre, knitting, rendered hyperreally down to her chapped knuckles and the fuzz of her yarn. Butter-tea steam curls around her into a halo-like aureole. Around her, in smaller hierarchical registers, float her worldly things: a thermos, a radio, prayer beads, a sleeping dog. Opaque layered colour in malachite green, cinnabar and lapis blue builds the scene. Every contour is retraced in fine gold-ochre pen line. A painted brocade border frames the whole like a silk mount.

A giant jawbreaker sweet cut cleanly in half, its face shown head-on and filling the frame edge to edge like a polished geode. Concentric sugar layers ring outward in translucent watercolour: cherry, lemon, lime, grape and opaque white. Each band is laid wet so the pigment blooms softly inside its ring, then held by a razor-crisp boundary where the next layer begins. The tiny crystalline sugar grit on the cut face is picked out with dry stippled pencil. The colours glow as if lit from behind, like a backlit stone slice. There is no background at all.

Seen from above on a black-painted farm table, real produce is laid out in a centre-diamond-in-a-square quilt layout. Black kale forms the outer border, then a band of deep plums. A diamond of halved red cabbage sits at the centre, and a single beet glows at its heart. Saturated watercolour gives aubergine, teal-green, garnet and plum their depth against a charcoal-mass ground. Fine graphite lines follow the veins and cut grain in looping, regular rhythms like quilting stitches. The light is plain and even, the mood sober and severe.

A sheet of kitchen aluminium foil, once folded into a crane and now flattened again, fills the whole picture plane. Its crease lattice of mountain and valley folds radiates in perfect origami geometry. A low raking light turns each facet a different steel tone, from bright mercury to near-graphite. The piece is drawn entirely in fine technical-pen hatching, with the direction of the lines shifting facet by facet like a faceted gem. Faint reflections of a window and a red mug warp across a few planes as the only colour. The edges are crumpled and torn.

A strict bird's-eye view of a square courtyard divided into four lawns by two narrow stone water channels that cross at a brimming octagonal fountain. Rendered like an architect's presentation drawing pushed into hyperrealism. Crisp graphite outlines carry every limestone joint and chipped edge. Transparent watercolour glazes build the clipped turf in sap green and olive. The rippling water picks up broken reflections of a cerulean sky and one overhanging pomegranate branch. The geometry is rigorously symmetrical, yet each quadrant hides one small disorder: a fallen fruit, a sandal, a wet footprint drying on the paving.

Rows of unglazed clay oil lamps are lined up on a woven tray, seen from straight above in a repeating stamp-like grid. Each lamp is hyperreal: thumb-pressed rims, soot on the wicks, a pool of ghee catching a highlight. They also behave like hand-block impressions. They are slightly misregistered row to row, some fainter and some doubled. The palette comes from Bagru's natural dyes: madder-alizarin red, iron-rust black, indigo shadow and mud-clay ochre. Textured watercolour fills carry a faint mottled bleed at their edges.

A split jackfruit fills the frame from a low angle. Its spiny rind, sticky latex threads and glossy golden bulbs are rendered in hyperreal detail, built entirely from Gond-style fills: dense rows of dots, dashes, chevrons and tiny crescents in fine pen. The fill direction follows each form's curve, so every spike and pod is modelled by the rhythm of its marks rather than by blending. Bright flat marker colour sits underneath: chartreuse rind, saffron flesh, a cobalt shadow side. The background is a saturated vermilion field.

A tall, mostly dark coloured-pencil drawing set on a ship's deck at dusk. A stemmed wine glass stands on a varnished teak rail. The final sliver of the sun is caught inside its bowl, refracted and inverted, flaring a sharp emerald-green bead at the rim of the liquid. Everything else is heavily burnished: indigo and Payne's grey sky, oxblood wine, teak grain rendered in layered umber strokes. The only pure green in the whole image is that tiny flash, so the eye is forced to hunt for it. Varnish highlights are lifted back as hard white specks.

A tall glass of fizzing cola over ice is drawn twice in pencil, once in cyan and once in red, offset sideways and overlaid. The result is a hyperreal anaglyph: condensation beads, carbonation trails and fractured ice all double into colour fringes. The offset is widest at the foreground straw and slices of lemon, and nearly converges at the back of the glass. Where the two layers coincide, they deepen to warm near-black. The paper is a cool newsprint grey. There is no other colour.

A hyperreal close view of a young woman's nape and shoulder, seen from behind. Powdered curls pin up in asymmetric C-scrolls, and a pale celadon silk ribbon loops and trails off the top edge. The palette is all Rococo confection: rose-blush skin, lilac shadow, buttercream highlight, pistachio silk. Soft spray and powdery pastel-like grain build the skin's peach fuzz and loose talc. Fine pencil defines individual stray hairs and the ribbon's woven sheen. The composition curls sideways, never centred, as if framed by an unseen gilt cartouche.

A close, frontal crop of a weathered pale-turquoise pickup truck grille and headlamp, presented as an unfinished paint-by-numbers board. About half the cells are filled with flat marker colour so precise and dense that the chrome, rust bloom and bug-spattered glass read as photographic. The rest stay bare cream card with thin printed cyan outlines and tiny numerals inside. The boundary between finished and blank cuts straight across the headlamp. A few cells are filled in the wrong colour, slightly over the line.

A pale plaster wall with real objects floating against it at steep, unsupported diagonals, arranged like Malevich's drifting planes. A single red clay brick, a black roofing slate, a cadmium-yellow sticky note and a long thin steel ruler hang at different tilts. Each object is rendered in exacting hyperreal detail: brick pores, slate cleavage, the curl of the note. Their faint, offset shadows on the wall are built in soft smudged charcoal. The wall itself is near-flat warm grey. The composition is asymmetric and weightless, leaning off the upper left.

A tall paint-sample card turned into hyperrealism. Seven hen eggs sit stacked in narrow horizontal bands, each egg filling its own chip. They grade from chalk white through cream, buff and terracotta to a speckled chocolate brown. Each band's background is a flat alcohol-marker field matched exactly to its egg's shell, so every egg almost dissolves into its swatch. Only soft cast shadows and pore-level speckling, built from fine felt-tip dots, pull it forward. A tiny ruled pen caption under each chip gives an invented paint name. The edges are knife-clean and the surfaces matte, like printed card stock.
